name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
summary: A unilateral bodyweight floor exercise that strengthens the glutes, hamstrings, and core by extending the hip on one leg while lying supine.

setup: Lie flat on your back on a mat with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, spaced hip-width apart.
Rest your arms straight along your sides with your palms pressed gently into the floor for support.
Lift one foot off the ground, either extending the non-working leg straight out or bending the knee toward your chest.
steps: Drive down firmly through the heel and midfoot of your working leg to lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Extend your hip until your thigh, pelvis, and torso form a straight diagonal line, actively squeezing your glute at the peak.
Hold the contraction at the top for a brief pause while keeping your pelvis square and level.
Lower your hips with control back down toward the floor until they lightly graze the mat, then immediately begin the next rep.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as you drive through your heel to lift your hips, and inhale as you lower back down with control.
cues: Lock out with the glute, not the lower back.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lumbar spine at the top of the movement.
common_faults.correction: Stop lifting once your torso and thigh form a straight line, keeping your ribs drawn down and abs engaged.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the pelvis to tilt or rotate toward the non-working side.
common_faults.correction: Brace your core and actively push both hip bones upward evenly throughout the repetition.

common_faults.fault: Placing the working foot too far forward or too close to the glutes.
common_faults.correction: Position the working heel directly beneath the knee so your shin is roughly vertical at the top.
